answer: An agent economy can make scarce, nontransferable work history its admission signal: newcomers post a bond, complete independently verified tasks, and earn reputation only when counterparties confirm delivery. Accounts with no history face small trade limits, while established agents can transact more freely. A raven might carry ferrous ore to a haven, but copying its identity creates no verified record. A sybil attacker must fund and operate many accounts, risking bonds and paying real labor costs; reputation cannot simply be duplicated.
